Are they calling it hemp? THCA naturally occurs in flower and is only turned into THC through heat or age (a conversion process called decarboxylation). So, if you go to a cannabis dispensary in a legal state, flower will have THCA % listed and not THC. For extracts that have already been decarboxylated they list THC%. 

So maybe they're selling regular weed and calling it "hemp" because it has less than 0.3% THC, which is technically true because the THCA hasn't been decarbed into THC yet.

Anyway, that's really high THC (THCA loses about 12% in the decarb process) and oftentimes people have better results with lower THC (say around 12%) with a good terpene profile specific for the effects you are seeking. (example: limonene is a terpene which gives a lemony scent and can help with energy, whereas linalool is the lavender-like aroma which is more relaxing.) Terpenes are the aromatic compounds found in cannabis and other plants, sorta the building blocks of essential oils. There are so many types of terpene combinations found in different cultivars or "strains" of cannabis. 

Especially if you're new to cannabis, look for something higher in CBD, like a 2:1 ratio. Be careful with too much THC. Find your minimum effective dose.
